original.question: Evaluate $\int\frac{x}{x^{2}+2x+2}\,dx$.
original.answer: Complete the square: $x^{2}+2x+2=(x+1)^{2}+1$. Let $u=x+1$, $x=u-1$, $du=dx$: $\int\frac{u-1}{u^{2}+1}\,du=\frac12\int\frac{2u}{u^{2}+1}\,du-\int\frac{1}{u^{2}+1}\,du=\frac12\ln(u^{2}+1)-\tan^{-1}u+C$. So the answer is $\frac12\ln(x^{2}+2x+2)-\tan^{-1}(x+1)+C$.
